questions.question: A colleague removes a person’s name but keeps their rare job title, exact date, and incident details. Is the text safe for course practice?

answers.text: Yes, removing the name makes all data anonymous.
answers.feedback: Other details can still identify a person.

answers.text: Yes, if Improve the model for everyone is off.
answers.feedback: Training settings do not remove identifiability or approval requirements.

answers.text: Not necessarily. Replace it with a fully fictional scenario.
answers.feedback: Indirect identifiers can identify someone. Use invented practice material.

answers.text: Yes, if the output will stay inside the business.
answers.feedback: The input is still shared with the tool. Intended output use does not settle privacy risks.

questions.feedback: Indirect identifiers can identify someone. Use invented practice material.

questions.question: ChatGPT cites a page for a New Zealand employment claim. What should the reviewer do?

answers.text: Accept it because it has a link.
answers.feedback: A citation can be wrong or fail to support the claim.

answers.text: Open the source, check the exact claim and date, and use the responsible qualified reviewer.
answers.feedback: Verify evidence and keep professional decisions with the responsible person.

answers.text: Ask ChatGPT to certify its own answer.
answers.feedback: The model’s assurance is not independent evidence.

answers.text: Check only whether the wording is easy to read.
answers.feedback: Readable wording is useful, but facts and consequences also need review.

questions.feedback: Verify evidence and keep professional decisions with the responsible person.

questions.question: Sensitive information was entered into an unapproved chat. What is the useful first response?

answers.text: Delete the chat and assume the matter is resolved.
answers.feedback: Deletion alone does not assess or resolve an incident.

answers.text: Keep using the chat to work out what to say.
answers.feedback: Stop the workflow to avoid further exposure.

answers.text: Put the full details into another public AI tool for advice.
answers.feedback: That could expose the information again.

answers.text: Stop the workflow and report through the organisation’s privacy or incident process.
answers.feedback: Tell the responsible manager or privacy officer promptly and follow the incident process.

questions.feedback: Tell the responsible manager or privacy officer promptly and follow the incident process.

questions.question: Select all elements that belong in the team policy starter.

answers.text: The approved tool, workspace, and allowed data.
answers.feedback: Staff need a clear account and information boundary.

answers.text: Who checks and approves relevant outputs.
answers.feedback: A named reviewer keeps accountability clear.

answers.text: Permission for ChatGPT to make final staff or financial decisions.
answers.feedback: Professional and people decisions must follow existing responsible review processes.

answers.text: An incident contact and a policy review date.
answers.feedback: Staff need a route to report problems, and rules need review as tools change.

questions.feedback: Staff need a clear account and information boundary. A named reviewer keeps accountability clear. Staff need a route to report problems, and rules need review as tools change.

questions.question: Match each review with what it checks.
questions.feedback: Use all three checks. An accurate draft can still require approval because of how it will be used.

answers.matchText: The output matches the original material
Amounts, dates, units, and claims are verified
The right person approves the intended use
